notes: FS19 has NO kick, ban, unban or broadcast command over any remote channel - those keys are omitted on purpose, not missing. The GIANTS dedicated server exposes an HTML admin web interface (default http://<ip>:8080/, login from the username/password in dedicatedServer.xml) that starts/stops the server and edits settings and mods but has no player-moderation control; kicking is done only from inside the game by a client that has logged in as admin with the admin password (ESC -> farm management -> admin login), which is a GUI action, not a text command. The in-game '^' console reached via game.xml <controls>true</controls> is a CLIENT cheat console (gsCheatMoney etc.) and cannot command a dedicated server - ignore hosting blogs that present it as server administration. What IS machine-usable is the read-only stats feed on the same web-interface port: GET /feed/dedicated-server-stats.json?code=<code> (also .xml), whose payload is {server, slots{capacity, used, players[]}, vehicles, mods, fields}; each player entry is {isUsed, isAdmin, uptime, name} when occupied and {isUsed: false} when the slot is empty. Consumers MUST discard entries with isUsed false - the schema's json playerParse has no filter for that - and note the feed exposes NO Steam ID or UID, only the display name, so the roster identifier is the username. Source disagreement: the .xml form of the feed is attested for FS19 by two independent projects (TheCoati/FS19-Java-API and TAEMBO/farming-simulator-types), while the .json form is attested for FS19 only by TAEMBO's typed routes; swap the extension to dedicated-server-stats.xml if a server 404s on .json. The 'code' is the web-statistics code shown by the server's own web interface; the dedicatedServer.xml setting that holds it was not confirmed, hence credentialSetting null. appId 787860 is the game: FS19 ships its dedicated server with the game rather than as a separate Steam app. Confidence low: the endpoint has two sources but the exact published command string (.json) and the payload field names rest on a single reverse-engineered code source, and GIANTS publishes no API documentation at all.
